mainTopic: צאן ברזל from a נכרי and בכורה: who owns the animals, יד גוי באמצע, and how many generations of young are exempt
overview: This עמוד finishes a משנה about a Jew who took sheep from a נכרי as צאן ברזל. In this deal the Jew raises the animals and guarantees their value to the owner. The young are exempt from בכורה because the נכרי can collect from them. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל extends the exemption even to ten generations. The משנה then teaches that a ewe that gives birth to a goat-like animal, or a goat that gives birth to a ewe-like animal, is exempt. The גמרא asks whether a צאן ברזל animal still belongs to its original owner, and it points to a contradiction with a משנה in בבא מציעא that calls such a deal ריבית. אביי answers by splitting the two cases according to who carries the risk. רבא rejects that answer and explains that the Jew owns the animals, but the exemption still applies because the נכרי can seize them (יד גוי באמצע). Finally, רב הונא and רב יהודה argue over how many generations are exempt. The גמרא defends רב יהודה against a challenge from the משנה and begins a challenge against רב הונא that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The young are exempt, but the grandchildren are obligated
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the direct young of צאן ברזל animals taken from a נכרי are exempt from בכורה. The young of those young are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their young are exempt from the firstborn law. The young of their young are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה, continuing the case of a Jew who took sheep from a נכרי as צאן ברזל, tells us which generation of babies is exempt from בכורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נכרי can collect his guaranteed value from the mother animals and from their direct young. Since the נכרי has a stake in that first generation, it is exempt. The next generation is fully the Jew's, so a firstborn male there is obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: 'iron sheep': an investment whose value is guaranteed to the owner

phrases.english: their young are exempt,
phrases.notes: "Their" means the sheep the Jew took from a נכרי as צאן ברזל. The earlier part of the משנה set this up.

phrases.english: the young of their young are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous daf about צאן ברזל taken from a נכרי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First-generation young of צאן ברזל from a נכרי are exempt from בכורה. The second generation is obligated.

steps.title: When the young are set up as the guarantee, the exemption goes one generation further
steps.stepSummary: If the Jew made the young the security in place of their mothers, the grandchildren are exempt and only the great-grandchildren are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he set their young in place of their mothers, the young of the young are exempt, and the young of the young of the young are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a twist. If the Jew made the babies stand in as the security instead of the mothers, the exemption moves down one generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the young have become the guarantee, the way the mothers were. That means their own young are the generation the נכרי can collect from, so that generation is exempt too. Only the generation after that is obligated.

phrases.english: If he set their young in place of their mothers —
phrases.notes: He means the Jew made the young the animals the נכרי can collect from, in case the mothers die.

phrases.english: the young of the young are exempt,
and the young of the young of the young are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule of step 1 to a case where the young replace the mothers as the security.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the young become the guarantee, the exemption moves down one generation.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: even ten generations are exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that every later generation is exempt, even down to ten, because all of them serve as the נכרי's guarantee.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: even up to ten generations are exempt, because the responsibility for them is to the נכרי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the תנא קמא and gives a much broader exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view the נכרי can collect from any animal descended from the original flock, however many generations down. So every generation stays tied to the נכרי, and none of them is obligated in בכורה.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
even up to ten generations are exempt,
phrases.notes: "Ten" is just a way of saying "as many generations as you like."

phrases.english: since their guarantee belongs to the gentile.
phrases.notes: In other words, the נכרי could collect his payment from any of these animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion's limit of one or two generations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All generations are exempt, because the נכרי's right to collect reaches all of them.
steps.whatToRemember: With צאן ברזל from a נכרי, the animals are exempt from בכורה because the נכרי still has a hold on them. The only argument is how many generations that hold reaches.

steps.title: A ewe that gives birth to a goat-like animal
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a ewe that gives birth to something that looks like a goat, or a goat that gives birth to something like a ewe, is exempt from בכורה. If the baby has some of its mother's features, it is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ewe that gave birth to a kind of goat, and a goat that gave birth to a kind of ewe, are exempt from the firstborn law. If the baby has some of the signs, it is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new topic: a firstborn that does not look like its mother's species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The firstborn law needs the baby to be the same kind as its mother. A baby that looks completely different does not qualify. If it shares some of its mother's features, it counts and is obligated.

phrases.english: A ewe that gave birth to a goat type,
and a goat that gave birth to a ewe type —
is exempt from the firstborn law,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין — חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: and if it has some of the signs — it is obligated.
phrases.notes: "The signs" are features that match its mother's species.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה on a different topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A baby of a different species from its mother is exempt from בכורה. If it shares some of the mother's features, it is obligated.

steps.title: Does the צאן ברזל animal still belong to the original owner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the צאן ברזל part of the משנה. It asks whether the משנה means the animal stays in the original owner's possession, since he has not yet been paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that since the owner has not taken his money, the animal stays in the owner's possession?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the משנה and checks it. This sets up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempted the animals because of the נכרי's connection to them. That suggests the נכרי, the original owner, still counts as the owner until he gets his money back. The גמרא states this as a question so it can test it.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Is this to say that since
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to the first part of the משנה, the צאן ברזל case.

phrases.english: the owner has not taken the money —
it stands in the owner's possession?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the צאן ברזל section (steps 1-3) and draws a principle from it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a צאן ברזל animal legally stay in the original owner's possession until he is paid?

steps.title: Contradiction: צאן ברזל from a Jew counts as ריבית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה that forbids taking צאן ברזל from a Jew because it is ריבית. That implies the animal belongs to the one who took it, the opposite of the inference in step 5.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: one may not take צאן ברזל from a Jew, because it is interest. So evidently the animal is in the receiver's possession!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference from step 5 with a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something can only be ריבית if it is a loan. A loan means the item now belongs to the borrower, who owes back its value. So the בבא מציעא משנה treats the צאן ברזל animal as the receiver's property, which clashes with our משנה's suggestion that it still belongs to the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: the receiver (the one who took the animals)

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
One may not accept צאן ברזל from a Jew
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בבא מציעא.

phrases.english: because it is interest,
evidently it stands in the receiver's possession!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the inference made in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a צאן ברזל animal stays in the original owner's possession.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling the deal ריבית means it is a loan, and a loan means the property has moved to the receiver. That contradicts our משנה's suggestion that the owner still holds it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. Our משנה is about צאן ברזל from a נכרי (the בכורה question). The challenge comes from a different משנה about צאן ברזל from a Jew (the ריבית question). The גמרא compares them only to ask who owns the animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: Who legally owns a צאן ברזל animal decides both whether it is exempt from בכורה and whether the deal is forbidden as ריבית.

steps.title: אביי splits the two cases by who carries the risk
steps.stepSummary: אביי says our משנה is a case where the gentile owner accepted the risk of accidents and price drops, so the animals stay his. The משנה in בבא מציעא is a case where the owner did not accept that risk, so the animals belong to the receiver.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There is no difficulty. This case is where he took on himself accidents and drops in value, and that case is where he did not take on himself accidents and drops in value.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction from step 6 by saying the two משניות are talking about two different deals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the original owner carries the risk of loss (אונסא) and of the price going down (זולא), the animals are still really his. That fits our משנה, where the offspring are exempt from בכורה because they belong to a נכרי. If the owner carries no risk, the animals belong to the receiver, and that is why the משנה in בבא מציעא calls it ריבית between Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no difficulty. This is how the גמרא opens an answer that splits two sources into different cases.
He took upon himself, meaning he accepted responsibility.
An accident or loss that is no one's fault, like the animal dying.
A drop in price or market value.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult.
This is where he accepted upon himself accidents and depreciation,
phrases.notes: 'This' is our משנה in בכורות, and 'that' is the משנה in בבא מציעא. 'He' is the original owner who gave out the animals.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא דְּלָא קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא.
phrases.english: and that is where he did not accept upon himself accidents and depreciation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the two משניות describe different deals.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seem to disagree about who owns צאן ברזל animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ownership depends on whether the original owner accepted the risk of אונסא and זולא.

steps.title: רבא: that is not called a guaranteed deal, and the משנה gives no such detail
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that if the owner carries the risk, the deal cannot be called צאן ברזל at all. He adds that the משניות state צאן ברזל plainly, with no sign of two kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If he accepted upon himself accidents and depreciation, do you call it 'iron sheep'? And furthermore, why does it say it without any distinction?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's answer with two objections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צאן ברזל means 'iron sheep': the owner's value is fixed and safe no matter what happens. If the owner carries the risk, his money is not safe, so the name does not fit. Also, both משניות use the term plainly (מאי פסקא), so how could it mean two different things?

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'iron sheep.' A deal where the receiver guarantees the full value to the owner, so the owner's investment is as safe as iron.
Why is it stated plainly, with no distinction? This asks why a source gives a flat rule if it really has two kinds of case.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Where he accepted upon himself accidents and depreciation,
you call that 'iron sheep'?
And furthermore, why is it stated without distinction?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: דְּקַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא, ״צֹאן בַּרְזֶל״ קָרֵית לֵיהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's split between a deal where the owner carries risk and one where he doesn't.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A deal where the owner carries risk is not called צאן ברזל, and the משניות give no sign of two different kinds.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה should have made the distinction inside the Jewish case
steps.stepSummary: רבא's third objection: if אביי were right, the משנה in בבא מציעא should not have contrasted Jew with נכרי. It should have said that even with a Jew the deal is allowed when the owner carries the risk.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, instead of teaching in the end of that משנה 'but one may accept צאן ברזל from a gentile,' let it make a distinction within the case itself and teach: When is this said? When he did not accept accidents and depreciation. But if he accepted accidents and depreciation, it is fine!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a third objection, based on how the משנה in בבא מציעא is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא of that משנה makes its contrast between a Jew and a נכרי. If a deal where the owner carries risk were also called צאן ברזל and were allowed, the easier contrast would be within the Jewish case. Since the משנה does not do that, it seems צאן ברזל has only one meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: Instead of teaching the last part of the משנה.
Let it make a distinction and teach it within the same case.
When is this said? A phrase that narrows a rule to certain cases.
It is fine, it is allowed.

phrases.english: And furthermore, instead of teaching in the latter clause,
phrases.notes: This is the end of the משנה in בבא מציעא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְקַבְּלִין צֹאן בַּרְזֶל מִן הַגּוֹי —
phrases.english: 'but one may accept iron sheep from a gentile,'
let it distinguish and teach within that same case:
phrases.notes: He means within the case of taking from a Jew.

phrases.english: When is this said?
When he did not accept upon himself accidents and depreciation,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא — שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי!
phrases.english: but if he accepted upon himself accidents and depreciation, it is fine!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, אַדְּתָנֵי סֵיפָא אֲבָל מְקַבְּלִין צֹאן בַּרְזֶל מִן הַגּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third objection against אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that a risk-bearing deal is a permitted kind of צאן ברזל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were true, the תנא would have taught the distinction within the Jewish case instead of contrasting Jew with נכרי.

steps.title: רבא: both משניות are the same case, with no risk on the owner
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops אביי's split. He says both משניות are talking about a real צאן ברזל, where the owner did not accept any risk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Both this and that are where he did not accept upon himself accidents and depreciation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts his own answer by saying both משניות describe the same kind of deal. This sets up his reason, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So in our משנה too, the animals really belong to the Jewish receiver, just as in בבא מציעא. This means the contradiction is gone, but now the גמרא must explain why the offspring in our משנה are still exempt from בכורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It shows the previous answer is being dropped.
Both this one and that one.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי דְּלָא קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא,
phrases.english: Both this and that are where he did not accept upon himself accidents and depreciation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's answer after רבא's objections.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Unifies the cases and moves the reason for the exemption somewhere else.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה exempts the offspring because the animals still belong to the נכרי.
steps.terutzMaskana: In both משניות the animals belong to the receiver. The exemption needs a different reason.

steps.title: Why the offspring are still exempt: the hand of a נכרי is in the middle
steps.stepSummary: Even though the animals belong to the Jew, if he does not pay, the נכרי can seize the mother or her offspring. That gives the נכרי a hold on them, and any animal where a נכרי has such a hold is exempt from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, regarding the firstborn, this is the reason: if the gentile came wanting his money and the Jew did not give it to him, he would seize the animal, and if he did not find the animal, he would seize its offspring. So the hand of a gentile is in the middle, and any animal where the hand of a gentile is in the middle is exempt from the firstborn law.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer and explains why the offspring in our משנה are exempt from בכורה, even though they belong to the Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נכרי does not own the animals, but he has a right to collect from them, even from the offspring, if he is not paid. This hold is called יד גוי באמצע. Any animal where a נכרי has this kind of hold is exempt from בכורה.

keyTerms.meaning: He seizes, he takes hold of it to collect his debt.
Literally 'the hand of a gentile is in the middle.' A נכרי has some hold on the animal, which exempts it from בכורה.
Exempt from the laws of a firstborn animal.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, צאן ברזל animals belong to the Jewish receiver. Their firstborn are still exempt because the נכרי can seize the mother or the offspring for his money. This is יד גוי באמצע, and any animal with יד גוי באמצע is exempt from בכורה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is saying the נכרי owns the animals. He is saying the opposite: the Jew owns them. The exemption comes only from the נכרי's right to seize them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a partial hold by a נכרי, even without full ownership, is enough to exempt an animal from בכורה.

phrases.english: And here, regarding the firstborn, this is the reason:
for if the gentile came wanting his money

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יָהֵיב לֵיהּ — תָּפֵיס לַהּ לִבְהֵמָה,
phrases.english: and the Jew did not give it to him, he would seize the animal,
and if he did not find the animal,
he would seize its offspring.
So the hand of a gentile is in the middle,
phrases.notes: He means the נכרי has some grip on these animals, even though he doesn't own them.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל יַד גּוֹי בָּאֶמְצַע — פְּטוּרָה מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה.
phrases.english: and wherever the hand of a gentile is in the middle, the animal is exempt from the firstborn law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer by giving the reason for the exemption.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason for the exemption that does not depend on who owns the animals.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The offspring are exempt only because the נכרי owns them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The offspring are exempt because the נכרי can seize them (יד גוי באמצע), even though the Jew owns them.

steps.title: The next line of the משנה: offspring set in place of their mothers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. If the Jew set the offspring in place of their mothers as security, the offspring of the offspring are also exempt from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he set their offspring in place of their mothers, the offspring of the offspring are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new line from the משנה to set up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 explained that the נכרי's power to seize the mother or her young exempts them from בכורה. Now the משנה adds a case: the Jew officially set the young in place of the mothers, so the נכרי can collect from them if the mothers die. In that case the exemption reaches even the grand-offspring.

keyTerms.meaning: He set up / established: he made the young stand in place of the mothers as the נכרי's security
Offspring (the direct young of the original animals)
Exempt (here, from the laws of בכורה)

phrases.english: If he set their offspring in place of their mothers
phrases.notes: He means the Jew made the young the נכרי's security, so if a mother dies, the נכרי can collect from her young.

phrases.english: the offspring of the offspring are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the basic צאן ברזל rule to the next clause of the משנה about later generations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the young are set in place of the mothers, the grand-offspring are also exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: רב הונא and רב יהודה argue over how many generations are exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says only the direct offspring are exempt, and their offspring are obligated. רב יהודה says the grand-offspring are also exempt, and only the third generation is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: the offspring are exempt, but the offspring of the offspring are obligated. רב יהודה said: the offspring of the offspring are also exempt, but the offspring of the offspring of the offspring are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים argue about how far down the generations the exemption from בכורה goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next step shows that this argument is about the ordinary case, where the Jew did not set the young in place of the mothers. רב הונא allows one exempt generation. רב יהודה allows two, which matches what the משנה said about the case where he did set them.

keyTerms.meaning: אמורא: only the first generation is exempt
אמורא: the first two generations are exempt

steps.confusionAlert: Count the generations carefully. 'ולדות' is the first generation, 'ולדי ולדות' is the second, and 'ולדי ולדי ולדות' is the third.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The offspring are exempt,
but the offspring of the offspring are obligated.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, reads 'וַולְדֵי וְלָדוֹת'.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
The offspring of the offspring are also exempt,
but the offspring of the offspring of the offspring are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an אמורא dispute about the generations mentioned in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: one generation exempt. רב יהודה: two generations exempt, the third obligated.

steps.title: The משנה's wording seems to refute רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה exempts the grand-offspring only when he set them in place of the mothers. That implies that without this, the grand-offspring are not exempt, which goes against רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if he set the offspring in place of their mothers, the offspring of the offspring are exempt. The reason is that he set them. But if he did not set them, they are not exempt. This is a refutation of רב יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה with a דיוק, an inference from the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ties the exemption of the grand-offspring to the act of setting the young in place of the mothers. So in the ordinary case, the grand-offspring should be obligated. רב יהודה said they are exempt even then, so the משנה seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is... (introduces an inference from wording)

phrases.english: We learned: If he set the offspring in place of their mothers,
the offspring of the offspring are exempt.
The reason is that he set them up,
but if he did not set them up — not.
phrases.notes: He means that without setting them up, the grand-offspring would not be exempt.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Rav Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יהודה's position from step 13 using the משנה from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that the grand-offspring are exempt even without העמיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes the grand-offspring's exemption depend on העמיד. So without העמיד they should be obligated.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the משנה means 'even if he set them up'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the rule is the same without העמיד. The משנה's point is that even with העמיד, the exemption stops after the grand-offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה can say to you: the same is true even if he did not set them up. And the משנה teaches us this: even if he set them up, it is also so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יהודה by reading the משנה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenger read the משנה as 'only with העמיד are the grand-offspring exempt.' רב יהודה reads it as 'even with העמיד, only the grand-offspring are exempt, not further generations.' So the משנה is limiting how far the exemption goes, not adding to it.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)
It teaches us (the new point being taught)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda can say to you:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא הֶעֱמִיד,
phrases.english: The same is true even though he did not set them up,
and this is what it teaches us:
even if he set them up, it is also so.
phrases.notes: Even with העמיד, the exemption still stops at the grand-offspring. It does not go on forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַב יְהוּדָה: הוּא הַדִּין
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה's wording (אפילו instead of only)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means only with העמיד are the grand-offspring exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means even with העמיד, only up to the grand-offspring are exempt.

steps.title: Why setting them up changes nothing
steps.stepSummary: A נכרי normally seizes the animal's offspring anyway. So setting them up is the same as not setting them up: the grand-offspring are exempt, and the next generation is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: For it is the way of a נכרי to seize her offspring, so it is as if he did not set them up. The offspring of the offspring are exempt, but the offspring of the offspring of the offspring are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב יהודה's answer by explaining why העמיד makes no difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Officially setting the young as security adds nothing new, because a נכרי would grab the young anyway. So the case with העמיד is just like the case without it. Both follow רב יהודה's rule: two generations exempt, the third obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: Like one who did not set them up

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יהודה, it makes no difference whether the young were set in place of the mothers or not. Either way, the first two generations are exempt from בכורה and the third generation is obligated.

phrases.english: For it is the way of a gentile to seize her offspring,
so it is like one who did not set them up:
the offspring of the offspring are exempt,
but the offspring of the offspring of the offspring are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רב יהודה's reading in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining that העמיד adds nothing to the נכרי's existing hold
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Setting the young as security might extend the exemption further.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since a נכרי seizes the young anyway, העמיד equals no העמיד. Two generations are exempt and the third is obligated.

steps.title: Quoting רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: even ten generations are exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה: even up to ten generations of offspring are exempt, because they are security for the נכרי. This quote will be the basis for a challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Even up to ten generations, the offspring are exempt, because the responsibility for them belongs to the נכרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the last line of the משנה, where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives his opinion. It is setting up a challenge that comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the exemption does not stop after one or two generations. It can go on as many as ten generations, because if the נכרי is not paid, he can collect from any of these animals. The key word is 'אֲפִילּוּ' (even), which hints that he is only stretching what the תנא קמא already said.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who disagrees with the תנא קמא in this משנה
Even. It shows he is adding on to an earlier view
Responsibility or liability. Here, the animals serve as security for the debt

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: We learned: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
phrases.notes: This is the very end of our משנה, the part right after the line quoted in Step 12.

phrases.english: Even up to ten generations, they are exempt,
since the responsibility for them is to the gentile.
phrases.notes: If the נכרי is not paid, he can collect from any of these animals. So the Jew does not fully own them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב יהודה (Steps 14–16), the גמרא now brings a source that will be used against רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא, who says only the direct offspring are exempt (Step 13)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'even' suggests that the תנא קמא already exempted several generations. That does not fit רב הונא's single generation.

steps.title: The quote fits רב יהודה, who says the תנא קמא goes into generations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a 'בשלמא' argument: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's wording makes sense according to רב יהודה, who holds that the תנא קמא already exempts more than one generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well according to רב יהודה, who says that the תנא קמא goes down into generations...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the משנה's wording fits nicely with רב יהודה. This is the first half of a 'בשלמא' line, and the turn to רב הונא comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה holds that the תנא קמא exempts two generations: the offspring and the grand-offspring. So it makes sense for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל to say 'even ten generations.' He is only adding to the number of generations both of them already accept. The implied problem is that רב הונא's view, with only one generation exempt, does not seem to fit this wording.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (according to this view). This sets up a 'but according to the other view, there is a problem'
Goes down / descends. Here it means the exemption extends into later generations
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This line is NOT a proof for רב יהודה standing by itself. It is the first half of a challenge. Its real target is רב הונא, and that part comes right on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav Yehuda, who says:
the first tanna went down into generations —
phrases.notes: The תנא קמא already exempts the grand-offspring too, as רב יהודה said in Step 13. The sentence continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the word 'even' from Step 17 to show the משנה fits רב יהודה. This sets up the problem for רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that only the direct offspring are exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תנא קמא already exempts several generations, then 'even ten generations' is a natural extension. According to רב הונא, the תנא קמא exempts only one generation, so the 'even' language is hard to explain.
